strings.name: Michelle Bachelet
strings.role: Former Chilean president · Former UN human rights chief
strings.summary: Bachelet trained as a doctor, endured detention and exile under Pinochet, and became Chile’s first female president, serving two terms. She pursued pension, education and gender equality reforms and led UN Women and the UN human rights office. Reform implementation, family-related controversies and her diplomacy toward China faced criticism. Her office released its Xinjiang assessment before she left in 2022; she withdrew her UN secretary-general candidacy in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Chile's first female president, she also led UN Women and served as UN high commissioner for human rights, influencing national and global governance.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Social policy reforms
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Pursued pension protection, educational access and gender equality reforms across two presidencies, with implementation still debated.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: International human rights leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Led UN Women and OHCHR, placing women’s participation and human rights within global governance.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Withdrew from the UN leadership race
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Withdrew her secretary-general candidacy, subsequently recorded by the UN, ending her bid for the post.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Released the Xinjiang assessment
strings.timeline.event-02.text: OHCHR released its assessment at the end of her term, after criticism from rights groups over her China visit and delays.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Became UN human rights chief
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Led OHCHR after her second Chilean presidency and left the office in 2022.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Began her second presidency
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Pursued tax and education reforms while an economic slowdown and controversies involving relatives added political pressure.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Appointed to lead UN Women
strings.timeline.event-05.text: After her first presidency, became the first executive director of the UN entity dedicated to gender equality.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Advanced pension reform
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Enacted legislation creating solidarity pension protection for people with insufficient individual savings.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Became Chile’s first female president
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Took office as the country’s first woman president and served until 2010.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Entered the cabinet
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Became health minister and moved to the defense ministry in 2002.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Completed her medical degree
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Resumed her studies at the University of Chile after returning from exile and graduated.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Detained and exiled
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Detained with her mother under military rule; after release, went into exile via Australia to East Germany.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Santiago
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Chile’s capital; her childhood included moves linked to her father’s military postings.
